description: The Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey of the U.S. Energy Information Administration is a periodic national sample survey of manufacturing establishments on their energy use. The 2022 survey's final results were released in stages to spring 2026; the release of 18 March 2026 added 12 tables on ratios of fuel consumption to economic characteristics, average prices and quantities of purchased energy, floorspace and building counts, and nine republished tables with hydrogen estimates by subsector and industry. Findings include that the chemicals subsector used the largest share of purchased electricity, natural gas and steam, that petroleum and coal products had the highest energy use per employee, that more than 40 percent of establishments ran energy management activities, and that under 1 percent had cogeneration. Tables are free downloads with highlight reports in PDF, and as U.S. Government works the data are in the public domain. Caveats: estimates are national or regional by industry, not per plant, and some cells are withheld for confidentiality or high sampling error. For simulation it provides the energy demand and fuel mix of manufacturing industries for energy-industry interdependency, demand and decarbonisation scenarios. Related catalogue records include Climate TRACE and the EPA Facility Registry Service.
